headline: Lynchburg finishes on top of the ODAC
dek: Lynchburg lost only two matches all season, recording sixteen wins and five draws across a campaign that reached late November. Unbeaten in conference play, the program was the ODAC's last side standing before Carnegie Mellon ended its run.

pattern.label: derived
pattern.text: Scoring in the ODAC separates into a high-output upper group and a tightly bunched lower tier, with Lynchburg's 52 goals outscoring Roanoke, Eastern Mennonite, and Averett combined.

wire.line: Averett went winless across fourteen defeats, scoring seven goals and conceding 88.

findings.label: observed
findings.text: Nine scheduled matches have passed their dates without a published result, including an all-conference meeting between Roanoke and Eastern Mennonite as well as non-conference dates for Guilford, Averett, and Randolph-Macon.

findings.label: observed
findings.text: Bridgewater goalkeeper Zane Kowalski stopped 51 shots while allowing ten goals, posting a 0.836 save percentage.

findings.label: observed
findings.text: Bridgewater forward Riley Queen paired eleven goals with ten assists across 56 shots, the only ODAC leader to reach double figures in both categories.

findings.label: observed
findings.text: Shenandoah recorded at least seventeen different goal scorers over the season, distributing its attack well beyond leading finisher Jarbin Rodriguez.

last_match.line: Lynchburg had gone unbeaten since early September and had not lost at home all season.

validation.policy: observed and derived claims are recomputed against the data home before publish; failures are dropped, not softened. signal and projected pass on schema unless the data contradicts a figure. context is never validated as a finding.
